items.heading: Indian pickles / Achar
details: Salt, acidity, oil, and drying together inhibit microbial growth, letting seasonal produce keep for months.

items.heading: Sun-dried papad
details: Reduced moisture from sun-drying inhibits microbial growth and extends storage life.

items.heading: Sun-dried vegetables
details: Removing moisture through sun-drying helps preserve seasonal vegetables well beyond their harvest window.

items.heading: Sun-dried chillies
details: Drying reduces water activity in the chillies, extending their storage life considerably.

items.heading: Aamchur (dried mango powder)
details: Drying raw mango and grinding it to powder reduces moisture, allowing long-term storage and use as a souring agent.

items.heading: Vadi / Vadagam preparations
details: Drying spiced lentil or vegetable mixtures allows seasonal ingredients to be stored for later use.

items.heading: Murabba
details: A high sugar concentration reduces water activity in the fruit, helping preserve it for extended periods.

items.heading: Fermented Indian foods
details: Microbial fermentation transforms many foods and can itself contribute to their preservation.

items.heading: Seasonal food drying
details: Preparing dried foods during suitable weather builds a longer-lasting food reserve for leaner seasons.
